newsitem.title: UK: Burnden Leisure up 30 pct on relisting.
newsitem.headline: Burnden Leisure up 30 pct on relisting.

text.p: Shares in Burnden Leisure Plc, owner of Bolton Wanderers football club, gained over 30 percent after the stock relisted on the London Stock Exchange after an eight-week break.
Burnden shares were up 16 pence, or 31.07 percent, to 67.5p by 0800 GMT in volume of 800,000 while the FTSE-100 index was 16.1 points, or 0.37 percent, higher at 4405.8.
Burnden closed at 51.5p on March 6. It changed its name from Mosaic Investments Plc in the interim after Mosaic acquired control of Bolton.

Bolton Wanderers also gained promotion to English football's elite premier league since Mosaic asked for its shares to be suspended on March 6, ensuring the club a share of lucrative television and sponsorship contracts.

While the name Burnden derives from the Bolton's current ground, Burnden Park, the club is seeking sponsors for the rights to the name of the new ground it will move into next season, beginning in August.
